title: Ordeo component layout
description: Describes the composition and layout of one component and its parts. Tokens hold the styling and every measure (gap, margin, inset); this file holds what the tokens cannot: which parts exist, what they hold, how they nest, and how they are placed and laid out. It is platform neutral and is consumed by tooling that generates the platform-specific code.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, so the IDE can validate the file.

components.description: Every renderable part of this component. The first entry is the root; the rest are the parts it (or another part) references through slots. Each entry becomes one component in the generated code.

part.description: One renderable part: the root or one of the parts it holds.

name.description: Unique name of this part in PascalCase; slots and other files refer to it by this name. By convention a part is prefixed with the name of the part that holds it, e.g. `ButtonIcon` inside `Button`.

tokens.description: Token paths (dot separated, as in the token files) whose styles apply to this part, e.g. `component.button.base`.

description.description: What this part is for, in prose, for whoever meets it without the file: why it exists, what it is measured against, and the decisions a reader would otherwise have to reconstruct from the tokens. It is the text a design tool shows beside the component and the comment a generator can carry into code, so it is written for a human and never restates the keys around it.

placement.description: Where this part is drawn inside whatever holds it, wherever it is placed. A slot's own `placement` overrides it. Omitted, the part is in the flow.

features.description: What kind of element this part is, beyond how it looks. Omitted, every feature has its default.

interactive.description: Whether this part is an interactive UI element: a control the user operates, such as a button, a link, a checkbox or a tab. `false`: the user reads or sees it but does not operate it, such as a label, an icon or a badge.

content.description: What this part renders. `none`: nothing but its own box, styled by its tokens, such as a divider, a track or a scrim. `text`: a run of text. `illustration`: a non-text visual such as an icon or a spinner. `image`: a picture the consumer supplies, such as a photo. `parts`: a container for other parts, filled through `slots`. The bare word is shorthand for `{ "type": <word> }` and is the form to use whenever there is nothing else to say; `parts` always has slots and so has no shorthand.

none-content.description: Nothing inside the part: what shows is its own box, drawn by its tokens (fill, border, radius, size).

text-content.description: A run of text the consumer supplies.

wrap.description: Whether the text breaks onto further lines when it does not fit. `false` keeps it on one line and ends it with an ellipsis, whatever `maxLines` says.

maxLines.description: The most lines the text takes while it wraps; the last one ends with an ellipsis. Omitted, the text takes as many lines as it needs.

name.description: The component this part draws, e.g. `Check` or `Spinner`; icons are components too. Omitted, the consumer picks what is drawn, and a preview shows a placeholder.

parts-content.description: A container for other parts, filled through its slots.

placement.description: Where a part is drawn: a placement, or conditions that pick one by variant.

placement-value.description: Where a part is drawn. `flow`: one of the parts its holder's `layout` arranges, sized and spaced with its siblings. `overlay`: taken out of the flow and drawn over the holder's box, where it takes no space and no gap; `inline` and `block` say where on the box it sits, its offsets come from tokens. The bare word is shorthand for `{ "type": <word> }` and is the form to use whenever there is nothing else to say.

inline.description: Where the part sits along the holder's inline axis (left to right in a left-to-right script).

block.description: Where the part sits along the holder's block axis (top to bottom).

layout.description: How this part arranges the parts in its slots. Only for parts whose content is `parts`; omit it when there is nothing to arrange. Gaps come from tokens. Every field but `type` may follow the variants through conditions.

stack-layout.description: Places the parts in a single line along `direction`.

justify.description: Distribution of the parts along the main axis.

align.description: Alignment of the parts on the cross axis.

wrap.description: Whether the parts move onto a further line when they do not fit.

phrase-layout.description: Sets the parts as one run of text, in slot order, the way a sentence is set. A `text` part continues the run: it breaks between words and wraps onto further lines. Any other part sits in the line as one piece, like a letter, and wraps with it. A slot that holds several parts adds them to the run one after another. The space beside a piece comes from tokens.

align.description: Where a piece that is not text sits against the line. `baseline`: on the text's baseline, like a letter. `center`: centred on the line.

grid-layout.description: Places the parts in rows of equal columns, in slot order, starting a new row when one is full.

columns.description: How many columns of equal width each row has.

justifyItems.description: Alignment of each part inside its cell along the row.

alignItems.description: Alignment of each part inside its cell across the row.

slots.description: Named places where the consumer supplies a part. Keys are the slot names in camelCase. An optional slot gets a switch named `show<Slot>`.

required.description: Whether the consumer must fill this slot.

for.description: What fills this slot: the name of a part in this file or of another component, or a list of them. The first entry is the default. `*` opens the slot to anything: alone, the slot has no default and a preview shows a placeholder; after a name (`["ButtonIcon", "*"]`), that part is the default and anything may replace it.

placement.description: Where the part in this slot is drawn, overriding the part's own `placement`.

sizing.description: How the part in this slot is sized while it is in the flow. In a `stack`, along its direction: `hug` is as big as its content, `fill` takes the space its siblings leave. In a `grid`: `fill` stretches it over its cell, whatever `justifyItems` and `alignItems` say; `hug` leaves it to them. While it is an overlay, its `inline` and `block` size it instead. A `phrase` sets its parts like letters, so its slots have no `sizing`.

multiple.description: Whether the slot holds a list of parts instead of one, such as the tabs of a tab list. The parts are laid out by the holder's `layout`, in the order the consumer gives them.

interaction.description: Whose interaction states (hovered, pressed, focused, …) the part in this slot shows. `inherit`: its holder's, so a card's title shows the card's hover. `own`: its own, because it takes input itself, like each tab of a tab list or a button inside a card; its own parts then inherit from it. A part takes input when it is the root or sits in an `own` slot.

description.description: What this place is for, in prose, for whoever fills it without the file: what belongs here, when to leave an optional slot empty, and what an open slot (`*`) expects. It is the text a design tool shows beside the slot and the comment a generator can carry onto its property, so it is written for a human and never restates the keys around it or the description of the part it holds.

image-content.description: A picture the consumer supplies, such as a photo or a thumbnail. Unlike an illustration it is content, so it needs a text alternative from the consumer.

fit.description: How the picture fills the part's box. `cover`: fills it and is cropped to it. `contain`: is shown whole, inside it.

overlay-alignment.description: `start`, `center` or `end` place the part at that side of the holder's box, at the size it takes. `stretch` spans the whole box: a bar along an edge is `stretch` on one axis and `end` on the other, a wash over the whole box is `stretch` on both.

variants.description: The axes the consumer picks on this part, such as `size`, `emphasis` or `align`, with the values it has, in the order the axis defines them. Most switch the part's tokens, but an axis need not. Interaction states are not variants; they are listed in `states`. Omitted, the part looks the same whatever its holder is set to.

states.description: The interaction states this part's tokens style. They follow the user's interaction and are not picked like variants. A part with none of them set shows its tokens' base style, so that is not listed.

slot-config.description: The variants the part in this slot gets from its holder. A list is shorthand for `{ "inherit": <list> }`. Only variants are configured: interaction states (hovered, pressed, …) are not variants and always follow the part's own interaction. Omitted, the part gets nothing from its holder.

inherited-axes.description: Axes the part takes from its holder unchanged, by name: the holder's `size` sets the part's `size`. `*` passes every variant axis the two share. An axis that is also set to a value is not inherited.

config-value.description: The value one axis of the part gets. A value fixes it, whatever the holder shows. Conditions pick it by the holder's variants: `{ "size=sm": "xs", "size=md": "sm" }` gives the part `xs` when the holder is `sm`. Every value of the holder's axes is covered; none passes unchanged, which is what `inherit` is for.

conditions.description: A value that follows the variants: each key is a condition, each value what the key takes when it holds. A condition is `axis=value`; `|` allows any of several values (`size=sm|lg`) and `,` joins axes that must all hold (`orientation=horizontal,align=start`). The axes are the `variants` of the part the value is written in: a slot belongs to its holder, so its `placement`, `sizing` and `config` follow the holder's. Every combination of the axes the conditions name is matched by exactly one of them: there is no default and no order.

block.description: Whether the part is a box of its own when it is placed in running text, such as a card, or sits in the line, such as a link or a badge in a sentence. `true`: it stands on lines of its own and breaks the text around it. `false`: a `stack` or `grid` sits in the line as one piece and moves with it (`inline-flex`, `inline-grid`); a `phrase` continues the text around it and wraps with it (`inline`). In a box, every part is a box. A part without a layout is in the line by its nature: text continues the run, anything else is one piece. It may follow the variants through conditions, such as a link that stands on its own.

variant-value.description: One value of an axis: a name such as `md`, or `false`/`true` for an axis that is on or off, such as `destructive`.
